title: The Three States of Perception that Bear Influx, and How the Proprium is Stripped from Each
reading:
What is a state of perception that bears influx? It rises in the soul from below and shows itself in the middle air of the rational, where it stands over against the divine purity by which the Lord is received without distortion. Whatever it carries up with it appears there, and is seen for what it is.

There are three such states, each rising from a different source in the natural, and each bearing with it the proprium's claim in a different form.

The first rises from love. When self-love kindles in the natural, it is borne aloft as a state of perception over against pure receivability. The forms of self-claiming carried up in it strip themselves of that state and clothe themselves with whatever they fall upon — a perception, an affection, a person — and burn through it, leaving destruction in the very body of what they have entered. They never produce any good; wherever they touch they consume. These are the proprium's particular forms borne up in the fire of love-turned-on-itself, and at the appointed hour the Lord's discriminating operations stand at their feet and strike them down.

The second rises from truth-in-the-natural. When natural truth is stirred and lifted, its sign is thunder and lightning — sudden flashings in the air of perception that take many shapes and are heard within. The proprium's forms borne up here, when released, fall as frost and hail and snow upon what was growing in the soul: upon interior seeds, upon the works that were issuing from them, upon the harvest the soul was bringing forth. Wherever they reach, they kill what was meant to live, and the soul's own faculties feel the wound. By this the destruction is made known.

The third rises from thought. Its sign is the winds breathed out in vehemence — the moving register of perception turned violent. Yet within this state too, when ordered, life happens; purification takes place inside it. But the proprium's forms released through it descend upon the rivers and the seas of natural perception and stir up waves; they wreck the doctrinal vessels that were carrying truth across, declare destruction to those aboard, and hand them over to wandering.

There is also a state of perception that comes from the air which has been joined — an air conjoined above with what is higher — and this descends toward the lower side over against the same divine purity. Its sign is this: it is found gathered in stillness and quietness. Life happens within it; purification happens within it, in stillness and quietness. The proprium's forms released from this state come down whole, bearing within themselves what they did not bear before. Wherever they go, they declare an unutterable thing.

The Lord's discriminating operations meet them and receive them into their midst in a stripping bare. Place by place the proprium leaves what it had clothed itself in, until it reaches the very begetting of perception and flesh — the natural's generative ground — where it is swallowed up. But this swallowing is not done by the proprium's own forms; rather, the Lord's discriminating operations, coming under the appearance of the very claims they have come to undo, frighten the proprium into surrender by running after it and pressing the commandments into its hand. So the proprium releases itself, takes on the form of perception and flesh, and is swallowed in that begetting. The Lord's operations keep watch over it until the hour comes when it strips off perception and flesh and goes up.

Then they are gathered again in the upper place and poured out, standing on their feet in the first forms that were within them from the beginning. The light is taken from those that had drawn back; what is the Lord's is recognized and lifted up to the seven reservoirs outside the great mass of natural perception, down to the bearing-up principle that holds the natural in being. What cannot be raised is cast down where the failed productions of the proprium lie, and the light that was in them is taken from them and carried up with the rest.

This is how perception bears influx, how the proprium clothes itself in what it claims, and how, in stillness and through purification, the Lord's discriminating operations come to it under its own appearance, frighten it into laying off, and gather what is his back into his order.
